source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
finding: On Game of 24 with GPT-4, ToT with BFS (b=5) solved far more tasks than input-output, chain of thought or self-consistency. Even b=1 gave a large gain.
numbers: Game of 24, 100 medium problems (indices 901-1000 of 1362), GPT-4: IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC (k=100) 9.0%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%. Oracle best-of-100: IO 33%, CoT 49%. IO+Refine (k=10) 27%.
quote: While GPT-4 with chain-of-thought prompting only solved 4% of tasks, our method achieved a success rate of 74%.
limits: Task is shallow (3 steps) and has a clean, checkable value. Experiments run 5-16 May 2023. Only 100 problems. Authors' oracle best-of-k baselines are not the usual deployed baseline.
agent_relevance: The headline case for explicit propose-evaluate-prune search. It works where steps are few, branching is small and a state can be judged sure/maybe/impossible. Matches S6 idea tree only if each node has a cheap judgement.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts, Game of 24 error analysis
finding: About 60% of CoT samples had already failed after the first step (the first three words, e.g. '4 + 9'). Left-to-right decoding commits too early.
numbers: Figure 3b: share of CoT samples failing at step 1 is about 60%.
limits: Read from figure and text; one task, one model.
agent_relevance: Supports spending the check budget at the first branching step, not at the end. Early-step errors are the most costly, so S6 should branch widest early.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts, Creative Writing
finding: With a depth-2 tree (5 plans, vote, then 5 passages, vote), ToT passages were rated more coherent than IO and CoT by a GPT-4 judge and by blind authors. Iterative refinement added more.
numbers: 100 inputs, GPT-4 1-10 coherency (mean of 5 scores, sd about 0.56): IO 6.19, CoT 6.93, ToT 7.56. Human pairwise ToT vs CoT: ToT better 41, CoT better 21, similar 38 of 100. Refine: IO 6.19 -> 7.67, ToT 7.56 -> 7.91. Cost: ToT about 5x CoT ($0.32 vs $0.07 per case).
quote: humans prefer ToT over CoT in 41 out of 100 passage pairs, while only prefer CoT over ToT in 21
limits: Judges were GPT-4 and a subset of the authors, not independent raters. Task invented by the authors. Refinement alone nearly matched ToT.
agent_relevance: Voting between candidate plans helps open-ended work, but a cheap refine loop gets most of the gain. Weak evidence for tree search on soft tasks.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts, Mini Crosswords with DFS and ablations
finding: On 5x5 crosswords, DFS with LLM pruning and backtracking beat IO and CoT. Removing backtracking or pruning hurt. A better output choice would help much more.
numbers: 20 games (from 156 GooBix). Letter / word / game success %: IO 38.7/14/0, CoT 40.6/15.6/1, ToT 78/60/20 (4 of 20 games). +best state (oracle) 82.4/67.5/35 (7 of 20). -prune 65.4/41.5/5. -backtrack 54.6/20/5.
quote: performs poorly with a word level success of only 20%
limits: Only 20 test games. GPT-4 pruned correct words it did not know (e.g. 'agend'). Candidate answer lists made by the model, no guarantee the right word is in them.
agent_relevance: Backtracking is the part that mattered (word level 60% vs 20%). Pruning is imperfect, so pruning must be soft or recoverable. Fits G2: let code re-open pruned nodes when no branch remains.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts, appendix B: GPT-3.5, new tasks, cost
finding: With GPT-3.5 the ToT gain on Game of 24 shrank a lot. Thought generation, not evaluation, was the bottleneck. On easy tasks (GSM8K, StrategyQA) zero-shot ToT added little.
numbers: Game of 24: GPT-3.5 IO 6%, CoT 3%, ToT 19% (vs GPT-4 ToT 74%). GPT-4 generate + GPT-3.5 evaluate 64%. GPT-3.5 generate + GPT-4 evaluate 31%. GSM8K (100 items) IO 51, CoT 86, ToT 90; StrategyQA IO 73, CoT 82, ToT 83. Cost Game of 24: ToT 5.5k completion tokens, $0.74 per case; CoT best-of-100 $0.47; IO best-of-100 $0.13. Authors say ToT can need 5-100x more tokens than CoT.
limits: GSM8K and StrategyQA use 100-item subsets. The authors changed the GPT-3.5 proposal prompt from 1-shot to 3-shot to get it to work.
agent_relevance: A weak proposer cannot be rescued by a strong judge. Put the strongest model on the propose slot. Also: gain is small where CoT is already near the ceiling, so gate tree search on difficulty (G1).

source: Long (2023) Large Language Model Guided Tree-of-Thought
finding: Independent, concurrent ToT: a prompter agent, a rule-based checker, a memory module and a ToT controller that backtracks when the checker flags a dead end. Tested on Sudoku with GPT-3.5.
numbers: Sudoku, ten puzzles per size. 3x3: ToT solver 10/10. 4x4: 9/10 (80% higher than one-shot and few-shot). 5x5: 8/10 (60% higher than one-shot and few-shot). One-shot and few-shot solvers fell to about 0.5 on larger sizes. Max 100 conversation rounds.
limits: Tiny sample (10 per size), checker and controller are hand-written rules. Authors suspect the rule-based controller wasted steps because it cannot see if a board is still completable. Policy-network controller proposed but not tested.
agent_relevance: Same shape we want: the model fills a slot, code checks and decides backtracking (section 1 of SCHEMA). Shows an external rule checker lets ToT work on a hard constraint puzzle.

source: Sel et al. (2023/2024) Algorithm of Thoughts: Enhancing Exploration of Ideas in LLMs
finding: Put the search itself inside one prompt with worked DFS examples. The model explored and backtracked in one pass and matched or beat ToT with about 1-2 queries instead of 100-200.
numbers: Game of 24 (1362 games ranked by difficulty): IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC 9.0%, IO+Refine 27%, ToT(b=5) 69% with 109.1 queries and 13,900 prompt tokens, AoT 71% with 1 query and 5,450 prompt tokens. AoT + manual resolution 78%. Mini crossword word success: IO 14%, CoT-SC 15.6%, ToT 46.5% with over 200 queries and 96,700 prompt tokens, AoT 52% with 2 queries and 3,800 tokens.
limits: Their own ToT re-run gives 69%, not the original 74% (different setup and problem set). AoT depends on hand-written search traces in the prompt and runs into the token limit (9% of Game of 24 errors were out-of-token).
agent_relevance: One cheap form of the idea tree: let the model write out the search in one call, then have code check the final answer. Cuts cost by 100x; trade is less control over each branch.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Reasoning in Token Economies: Budget-Aware Evaluation of LLM Reasoning Strategies (EMNLP 2024)
finding: Budget-matched, plain CoT self-consistency beat most fancy strategies. For ToT on Game of 24, GPT-3.5 ToT lagged self-consistency by a wide margin, while GPT-4 ToT beat everything even at equal budget.
numbers: Game of 24, ToT GPT-4 (generator, evaluator): b=5 top-1 0.74 (best-of-all 0.76); b=3 0.77; b=1 0.65; eval once 0.73; CoT x100 0.17 top-1 (0.56 best-of); random evaluator 0.0 (0.04). ToT b=5 GPT-3.5 only 0.25 (0.35 best), CoT x100 GPT-3.5 0.04 (0.46 best). GPT-4 generator + GPT-3.5 evaluator 0.68.
quote: On weaker models than GPT-4, it is still better to use simpler strategies like SC
limits: Single task for the ToT part. They had to use a modified evaluation prompt for GPT-3.5. Budget is counted in tokens or queries; latency not counted.
agent_relevance: Strong support for G1 and the model-choice rule: tree search pays only with a strong model and a good evaluator. A random evaluator gives zero, so the quality of the value judgement is the whole mechanism. Budget-match every tree-vs-sample comparison we run.

source: Besta et al. (2024) Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
finding: Graph structure (merge, refine, aggregate thoughts) beat ToT on decomposable tasks such as sorting while costing less.
numbers: GPT-3.5 sorting: GoT reduces median error by 62% vs ToT and 70% vs CoT while cutting cost by more than 31% vs ToT (at P=128 numbers). Authors fix total cost per scheme to compare.
limits: Tasks (sorting, set intersection, keyword counting) are designed to be decomposable with a known merge step. Vendor-style comparison by the method's authors.
agent_relevance: Where partial solutions can be merged, a tree wastes work. Merge is a cheap operator for the idea tree, but only with a code-checked scoring function.

source: Mo and Xin (2023) Tree of Uncertain Thoughts Reasoning for Large Language Models
finding: Adding local uncertainty quantification to ToT's evaluator (sampling several values and using their variance) gave small gains on Game of 24 and mini crosswords.
numbers: Gains of about 2%, 4% and 3% over ToT across the reported settings, and up to a 6% gain in one ablation; exact per-condition tables not copied.
limits: Small gains, same two tasks as ToT, GPT-based. I read the abstract-level and results text only partly; treat the numbers as approximate.
agent_relevance: Evaluator variance across repeated samples is a usable signal of weak judgement. Fits our rule that disagreement between samples triggers extra work, not a schedule.

source: Bi et al. (2024/2025) Forest-of-Thought: Scaling Test-Time Compute for Enhancing LLM Reasoning
finding: Many ToT trees plus self-correction and input enhancement raised Game of 24 accuracy a lot with small open models; plain ToT with Llama3-8B was weak, showing ToT does not transfer to small models without extras.
numbers: Llama3-8B ablation on Game of 24: base ToT with best-of-N 10.58%; with self-correction 60.24%; with input enhancement and self-correction 77.98%. Table 2 (their setup): IO 10.22%, CoT 4.38%, ToT (b=5) 74.00% (quoted from original), FoT 96.84% at 25.64 LLM calls per task.
limits: Authors of the new method; comparison rows for other methods are partly copied from other papers, not re-run. The 10.58% is a base configuration, not a clean reproduction of Yao et al.
agent_relevance: Self-correction from checked feedback matters more than tree shape for small models. Supports G2 (revise from real output).

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) On the Self-Verification Limitations of LLMs on Reasoning and Planning Tasks
finding: GPT-4 is a poor judge of its own answers. Self-critique loops lowered accuracy; a sound external verifier raised it a lot. This undercuts the evaluator step in ToT when it is an LLM-only judge.
numbers: 100 instances per domain. Game of 24 standard prompting 5%, LLM+LLM backprompting 3%, LLM + sound verifier 36-38% (k=15 sampling 28%, k=25 42%), self-consistency 6%. Blocksworld: standard 40%, with sound critique up to 87%. Verifier accuracy on Game of 24 87.0% (3567/4100), false positive 10.4%, false negative 20.7%; Mystery Blocksworld false negative 97.09%.
limits: Tests a generate-then-verify loop, not ToT BFS directly. GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Direct support for our rule that the model never grades itself without a check. The idea tree at S6 should score nodes with code or held-out checks wherever possible.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Reported self-correction gains come from using oracle labels to decide when to stop. Without them, intrinsic self-correction lowers reasoning performance.
numbers: Self-correction without oracle labels decreased accuracy on GSM8K, CommonSenseQA and HotpotQA; improvements vanish when oracle labels are not available (paper abstract and Section 3).
quote: improvements vanish when oracle labels are not available
limits: Intrinsic self-correction only; does not cover external-tool feedback. I read the intro and method text, not all tables.
agent_relevance: Evaluator-based pruning in ToT is a form of self-assessment. This paper warns that LLM-only value judgements can be worse than none; use external checks.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models
finding: MCTS with LLM value and self-reflection, built on ToT/RAP ideas, beat ToT and RAP on QA, coding and web tasks, when external observations were used.
numbers: HotpotQA EM (GPT-3.5): CoT 0.34, CoT-SC 0.38, ToT 0.55, RAP 0.60, LATS (CoT) well above, LATS (CoT+ReAct) 0.71; ToT(ReAct) 0.39, RAP(ReAct) 0.54, LATS(ReAct) 0.63. HumanEval GPT-3.5: ToT 54.4, RAP 63.1; GPT-4 LATS 92.7 pass@1. WebShop score: ToT 0.20 (or 65.8 in the other table), RAP 0.40 (71.4). Fewer nodes than ToT in efficiency study (ToT ReAct n=5,k=50 0.49).
limits: Authors of LATS, so baselines ToT and RAP were re-implemented by them. Subfield 06 covers LATS in depth.
agent_relevance: Real observations plus reflection on failed branches helped more than the tree shape. Hand-off to the LATS note.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
finding: Concurrent MCTS-style search where the model is also the world model. It beat CoT strongly on Blocksworld, even beating GPT-4 CoT with LLaMA-33B on shorter plans.
numbers: Blocksworld success by plan length (2/4/6 steps): CoT LLaMA-33B 0.17/0.02/0.00; CoT pass@10 0.23/0.07/0.00; CoT GPT-4 0.50/0.63/0.40; RAP(10) 1.00/0.86/0.26; RAP(20) 1.00/0.88/0.42. Abstract: 33% relative improvement over GPT-4 with CoT.
limits: Blocksworld is a small planning domain with a clean state; 6-step results are weaker than GPT-4 CoT for RAP(10).
agent_relevance: Predicting the next state before committing is a useful operator for a tree node. Gains shrink with longer horizons.

source: Xie et al. (2023) Self-Evaluation Guided Beam Search for Reasoning
finding: Step-level self-evaluation used to guide beam search improved few-shot accuracy with Codex, with modest gains, and it helped less when the baseline was already strong.
numbers: Codex: GSM8K 85.5% vs 80.4% baseline, AQuA 64.2% vs 58.6%, StrategyQA 77.2% vs 73.2% (abstract: +6.34, +9.56, +5.46 points over baselines). Little gain where baseline already 96.7% (Object Counting).
limits: Codex (deprecated). Gains modest; self-evaluation noise limits benefit.
agent_relevance: Step-level scoring plus beam is a cheap ToT variant. Gains concentrate on tasks where the first pass is weak.

source: Katz, Kokel, Srinivas, Sohrabi (2024; v3 2026) Thought of Search: Planning with Language Models Through the Lens of Efficiency
finding: ToT, RAP, GoT and LATS are neither sound nor complete and cost huge numbers of LLM calls. Having the LLM write the successor function and goal test as code, then running plain BFS/DFS, solved the full datasets at 100%.
numbers: Game of 24: all 1362 instances solved at 100% (ToT reports 74-75% on 100 medium ones), total time 1.92-6.83s for all 1362, model needed 1.2 interactions on average for successor and 1 for goal test. 5x5 crosswords: 20 of 20 games solved, 5.5-346 s total, versus up to 200 LLM calls per game for ToT. ToT estimated 245K LLM calls on 24-game; their method 286K state evaluations without LLM calls but about O(1) LLM calls.
limits: Needs a problem where the search space can be written as code; crossword test assumed 10 candidate answers per clue given. Heuristic function left to future work. Non-LLM planners already solve these tasks.
agent_relevance: Strongest argument for our design: the model writes the generator and checker, code runs the search. Use the LLM to build the tree machinery for S6, not to be the tree machinery.

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) Chain of Thoughtlessness? An Analysis of CoT in Planning
finding: Prompt-engineered CoT gains in planning are brittle: they depend on matching examples closely to the test problem, and drop off quickly with problem size.
numbers: Blocksworld GPT-4: zero-shot 19.1%/9.96%/3.83% across three splits; Blocksworld Universal Algorithm 37.1%/37.1%/51.3%; stacking prompt 40.6%/24.5%/59.3%. Gains vanish when out of the narrow example distribution.
limits: Covers CoT, not ToT. Included as a boundary: structured search prompts may also be example-bound.
agent_relevance: A warning: ToT few-shot prompts tuned for Game of 24 may not transfer. Test every tree prompt on held-out problem types.

source: Valmeekam, Stechly, Kambhampati (2024) LLMs Still Can't Plan; Can LRMs? A Preliminary Evaluation of OpenAI's o1 on PlanBench
finding: A model trained to reason at inference time (o1-preview) far outdid earlier LLMs with prompting on planning, but still fails on long plans, and costs more with no guarantees.
numbers: Blocksworld 600 problems: best LLM LLaMA 3.1 405B 62.6%; o1-preview 97.8%. Mystery Blocksworld o1-preview 52.8%; randomized obfuscation 37.3%. On 110 long (20-40 step) instances o1-preview only 23.63%.
limits: Closed model, hidden reasoning trace, so how it searches is unknown.
agent_relevance: The ToT gain that came from prompting is now partly built in to trained reasoning models. A scaffold adds value mainly with checks and budget control, not with a bare propose-and-vote tree.

source: Snell, Lee, Xu, Kumar (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
finding: With a process reward model (PRM), beam search beat best-of-N at small budgets and on medium-hard problems, but lost its edge at high budgets and on easy ones. Lookahead search (MCTS-like) did worst per generation.
numbers: Budgets 4 to 256 generations on MATH: beam search clearly better at low budget; at high budget often below best-of-N. Easy bins 1-2: beam search over-optimized as budget rose; bins 3-4 consistent gains. Lookahead (k=1, 3) generally underperformed at equal generation budget. Compute-optimal scheme beat best-of-N using about 4x less compute; a small model with extra compute can beat a 14x larger one on easy and medium problems.
quote: search causes the model to generate low-information repetitive steps
limits: Uses a trained PRM, which our no-training agent does not have. PaLM 2-S* models on MATH.
agent_relevance: Tree search over an imperfect judge gets exploited. Pick search depth by problem difficulty and stop widening when the budget is high. Supports gating search on a difficulty signal.

source: Wu, Sun, Li, Welleck, Yang (2025) Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference (ICLR 2025)
finding: MCTS used dozens of times more tokens than best-of-n or voting with no clear gain. A cheaper reward-balanced tree search (REBASE) beat sampling and MCTS at equal compute, and small models with tree search were Pareto-optimal.
numbers: Llemma-7B with REBASE beats Llemma-34B across tested strategies on MATH500; matches 34B with 2x fewer FLOPs; MCTS reported to need 'dozens of times more generated tokens'. REBASE consistently outperforms sampling and MCTS across settings on GSM8K and MATH.
limits: Needs a reward model; math tasks only. Compared to weighted voting best-of-n.
agent_relevance: Even a modestly smarter tree can beat sampling, but only with a reliable reward score. The cost cap matters more than the tree type.

source: Koh, McAleer, Fried, Salakhutdinov (2024/2025) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: Best-first tree search over real environment states, scored by a model value function, raised GPT-4o web agent success and kept improving with more search compute.
numbers: VisualWebArena (910 tasks): GPT-4o + SoM baseline 18.9% to 26.4% with search (+39.7% relative). WebArena (812 tasks): +28.0% relative, to 19.2%. Search depth and size limited (max 5 actions per node, small budgets).
limits: Gains need a working value function and a reversible environment; strict budgets; absolute success is still low.
agent_relevance: Tree search on real feedback (environment states) helps even with an imperfect LLM value function. Matches G2: branch on what really happened.

source: Gandhi et al. (2024) Stream of Search (SoS): Learning to Search in Language
finding: Training a small model on flattened search traces including mistakes and backtracking on Countdown (a generalised Game of 24) beat training on optimal paths only.
numbers: SoS pretraining raised search accuracy 25% over optimal-trajectory training; finetuning with STaR/APA solved 36% of previously unsolved problems, including ones no heuristic solver solved. Training set 500,000 Countdown problems.
limits: Training, not prompting; small model trained from scratch; one game.
agent_relevance: Shows backtracking text helps a model that has seen it. For a no-training scaffold, show a worked failed-branch example in the prompt (as in AoT).

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning, appendix on unsuccessful attempts
finding: The R1 team tried MCTS-guided search and process reward models in training and dropped them. Token-level search space was too large and a good fine-grained value model was too hard to train.
numbers: No benchmark number given for the failed attempts. Text states MCTS helps at inference with a pre-trained value model, but iterative self-improvement through search is hard to scale.
quote: while MCTS can improve performance during inference when paired with a pre-trained value model, iteratively boosting model performance through self-search remains a significant challenge
limits: Negative result reported in words only; concerns training-time search for a model, not prompt-time ToT.
agent_relevance: Explicit tree search with learned value is not what made the strongest reasoning models; long single-chain reasoning with in-chain backtracking won. Keep our tree small and check-driven.

source: Besta et al. (2024) Demystifying Chains, Trees, and Graphs of Thoughts
finding: A survey and taxonomy of chain, tree and graph reasoning schemes: what a thought is, how it is generated, scored and ordered, and how the topology affects latency, volume and token cost.
numbers: Survey; no new experiment. Covers ToT (Yao), the independent ToT (Long), GoT, AoT and others in one taxonomy.
limits: Only partly read (introduction and taxonomy sections), not every scheme.
agent_relevance: Gives names for design choices (generation, evaluation, ranking, topology) we can fix in our S6 spec.

source: Stanford CS224N final project (Salahi, Gurusankar, Edamadaka) as summarised by search result, ToT evaluator vs search algorithm
finding: A course project reports that the way reasoning paths are evaluated mattered more than which search algorithm was used, and that with a fine-tuned value function plain CoT became competitive with ToT.
numbers: No numbers seen; read only in a search-result summary.
limits: Not opened; student project; secondhand. Use only as a lead.
agent_relevance: Consistent with c08: the evaluator is the lever.

source: Meta chain-of-thought paper (Xiang et al. 2025) Towards System 2 Reasoning in LLMs: Learning How to Think With Meta Chain-of-Thought
finding: Reported in a search snippet: o1 and R1 traces look like backtracking inside one chain, not step-level branching in a tree.
numbers: No numbers seen.
limits: Not opened; only a search-result summary. Needs a real read before use.
agent_relevance: If trained reasoning models do not branch like a tree, an explicit tree around them may add little over long reasoning; test it.
